headline: Kananaskis Conservation Pass required for all vehicles
reservation: A Kananaskis Conservation Pass is mandatory for all vehicles parked within the park and Kananaskis Country; this is separate from any camping fees. While day-use trail access does not currently require a timed entry slot, front-country campsites often fill months in advance through the Alberta Parks system. Visitors should verify the latest pass requirements and seasonal road closures on the official Alberta Parks website before departure.

days.title: Glacial Lakes and High Alpine Vistas

stops.name: Upper Kananaskis Lake
stops.detail: Walk the shoreline trail to view the surrounding peaks reflected in the glacial waters.

stops.name: Rawson Lake
stops.detail: Ascend the forested trail to reach this high-elevation cirque nestled beneath Mount Sarrail.

days.driving: Allow 45–60 minutes; conditions vary by weather.
days.note: High elevation trails may remain snow-covered until mid-summer.

days.title: Upper Highwood Pass Exploration

stops.name: Ptarmigan Cirque
stops.detail: Trek through one of the highest accessible meadows in the Canadian Rockies for alpine flora and fossils.

stops.name: Highwood Pass
stops.detail: Observe the transition of the subalpine forest at the highest paved pass in Canada.

days.driving: Allow 30–50 minutes; pass access is seasonally restricted.
days.note: Check the status of Highway 40, which closes annually for wildlife migration.

days.title: Lowland Meadows and Lower Lakes

stops.name: Lower Kananaskis Lake
stops.detail: Explore the diverse wetlands and paved cycling paths connecting the various day-use areas.

stops.name: Elbow Lake
stops.detail: A short, steep hike leads to the headwaters of the Elbow River and views of the Rae Glacier.

days.driving: Allow 40–60 minutes; travel times vary with wildlife sightings.
days.note: Bears are frequently active in the valley; carry deterrents and check trail reports.

intel.title: Trailhead Capacity
intel.text: Lot sizes vary significantly between the popular Upper Lake and remote Highwood areas. Many visitors arrive early to secure space at the primary glacial lake trailheads.

intel.title: Remote Connectivity
intel.text: Cellular service is extremely limited or non-existent once you enter the Kananaskis Valley. Download offline maps and emergency information in Canmore or Calgary before arrival.

intel.title: Kananaskis Supply Points
intel.text: Fuel is available at Fortress Junction, but availability can fluctuate seasonally. It is advisable to fill your tank in Canmore or Longview before entering the park interior.

intel.title: Seasonal Road Closures
intel.text: Highway 40 through Highwood Pass is closed to vehicles from December to mid-June. Plan visits to the southern sections of the park for late summer or early autumn.

intel.title: Kananaskis Conservation Pass
intel.text: Purchase your pass online or at a visitor center to avoid penalties at trailheads. The pass is linked to your license plate and is monitored by park enforcement.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental at Calgary International (YYC), stock up on mountain supplies in Canmore, and ensure you have purchased your conservation pass before entering the park gates.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are sufficient for paved areas, but higher clearance may be beneficial for certain trail access roads; check rental agreements for gravel road restrictions.
plan.goldenHour: Rockwall viewpoints at Upper Kananaskis Lake, best viewed during late summer sunsets when light hits the peaks.
